subject: Agriculture
title: Can Organic Feed the World?
description: A micro-lesson that makes Can Organic Feed the World? usable.

hook.text: If all farming went organic tomorrow, would the world starve? The answer depends entirely on what else changes.

buildup.text: Pure yield comparison says no—organic produces 20% less. We'd need 20% more farmland or feed 20% fewer people.

discovery.text: But 30% of food is wasted. 36% of grain feeds animals, not humans. The system, not just the yield, is the problem.

twist.text: A 2017 study found 100% organic is feasible if food waste drops 50% and animal feed from cropland drops by a third.

climax.text: The question isn't 'can organic feed the world?' It's 'can organic feed the world we're willing to build?'

punchline.text: Organic can feed everyone—if we change what 'everyone eats' looks like.

quiz.question: Under what conditions could 100% organic farming feed the world?
options: If food waste drops 50% and feed crop use is reduced
